paper_metadata.title: Real Option Pricing using Quantum Computers

summary: The paper proposes a derivative‑pricing pipeline combining a new direct payoff encoding with modified Real Quantum Amplitude Estimation (mRQAE). Experiments on a quantum emulator (QLM on CESGA’s Finisterrae III) use a 32‑point discretized Black‑Scholes distribution encoded with 5 qubits (+1 ancilla) and show that mRQAE can recover the correct sign of expected payoffs while maintaining the O(1/ε) scaling advantage of amplitude estimation over classical Monte Carlo’s O(1/ε²). All results are simulator‑based demonstrations of theoretical quadratic speedup.

experiments.description: Quantum accelerated Monte Carlo pricing of European call, put, and digital options using square-root encoding and modified iterative quantum amplitude estimation (mIQAE) on a quantum emulator, with Black-Scholes state preparation.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Accelerated Monte Carlo (QAMC) with square-root encoding and mIQAE
algorithm.convergence_criteria: target precision ϵ for amplitude estimation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Black-Scholes probability distribution discretized on 32 points and loaded into a single register; payoff encoded via square-root encoding into an ancilla qubit
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate discounted expected payoff E[F(S_T)|F_t] via amplitude estimation

problem_instance.description: European option pricing under Black-Scholes dynamics for vanilla call, put, and digital payoffs

dataset_specification.description: risk-free rate 0.01, volatility 0.5, maturity 1 year, initial underlying value 1.0, discretized on 32 points between 0.01 and 5.0

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Exact Black-Scholes simulation; discretization of the terminal distribution into 32 points
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Absolute error between QAMC estimate and discretized expectation versus number of oracle calls; medians with 25th and 75th percentiles shown in Figure 5

hardware.device_name: QLM QAPTIVA emulator on Finisterrae III

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Black-Scholes distribution discretization and payoff normalization
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Convert estimated probability to option price using normalization constants

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: error versus oracle calls; no training loss

results.uncertainty: Figure 5 reports medians with 25th/75th percentiles, but exact numeric values are not stated in the text provided.

speedup_claims.conditions: Amplitude estimation on the QAMC pipeline; asymptotic scaling in oracle calls
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper notes that the quantum oracle cost is comparable to one classical path simulation, and the advantage is in the 1/NQ vs 1/sqrt(NC) sampling scaling.

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: not reported; theoretical quadratic speedup only
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: hundreds to thousands of logical qubits and deep Grover-style circuits according to the discussion in Section 4
limiting_factors: current gate error rates and decoherence

notes: Figure 5 and Section 2.2.3 report the 32-point Black-Scholes discretization requiring 5 qubits.
Hardware is a quantum emulator / QLM software stack on CESGA infrastructure, not a real QPU.
Paper explicitly states only theoretical quadratic speedup of QAMC over classical Monte Carlo.
